newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot propane retraces late, EIAs awaited.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot propane retraces late, EIAs awaited.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices retraced intraday losses in late Wednesday trade following a rise in NYMEX futures and strong crop drying demand in the Midwest, traders said.
Cold weather and rains in the Midwest also added to the afternoon bullishness since many rural homes use propane as a home heating fuel.

Traders said that about 300,000 barrels per day of propane were being pulled from pipelines in the Midwest for drying the corn crop, which is less than 50 percent harvested and has a high moisture content.
After falling about 1.25 cents this morning, Conway, Kansas, hub propane regained about one cent to between 55.50 cents and 55.75 cents a gallon in active trade.
The U.S. Gulf Coast, which fell one cent this morning, edged up a quarter cent to 53.75/54.00 cents.
The Gulf rose partly on the strength of Conway and the slight comeback of NYMEX December crude oil futures.

Meanwhile, players said they were were predicting about an 800,000 to one million barrel build in the Gulf Coast in tonight's EIA stock data report. Anything below would have a bullish impact on the market.
Conway traders said they expected a one million barrel draw in the week due to crop drying demand.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
